sec: Treatment regimens, culture-negative disease, surgery, prophylaxis

items.q: Streptococcus viridans regimen — match — 1) DOC 2) Alternative 3) If penicillin resistant … A) Ceftriaxone 2 g IV once daily or vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD B) Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD C) Penicillin G 2-3 million units IV every 4 hours for 4 weeks
items.exp: 'Streptococcus viridans : DOC : Penicillin G 2-3 million units IV Q4h × 4 wks. Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD × 4 wks OR Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD (if Penicillin resistant : vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD × 4-6 wks)'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Enterococcal regimen — match — 1) Base drug 2) Synergy 3) Penicillin-resistant option … A) Gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV TDS B) Penicillin G 4-5 million units Q4h × 4-6 wks C) Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD × 4-6 wks
items.exp: 'Enterococci : Penicillin G 4-5 million units Q4h × 4-6 wks; Gentamicin (1 mg/kg IV TDS); (if Penicillin resistant : vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD × 4-6 wks)'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Which organisms are printed as intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins?
items.exp: 'Note : Intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins · Enterococci, · Listeria'. (Book p1052)

items.q: MRSA endocarditis — match — 1) Native valve 2) Prosthetic valve … A) Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD plus gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV BD plus rifampicin 300 mg orally TID for 6-8 weeks B) Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD
items.exp: 'Native valve : vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD × 4-6 wks'; 'Prosthetic valve : Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV BD + Gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV BD + Rifampicin 300 mg oral TID × 6-8 wks'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Dose and duration printed for rifampicin in prosthetic-valve MRSA endocarditis?
opts: 300 mg orally three times a day for 6 – 8 weeks

items.q: Culture-negative endocarditis — match — 1) Culture report negative 2) True culture negative … A) Rare condition, no prior antibiotics, treated with vancomycin plus gentamicin for 4-6 weeks B) Common condition, prior antibiotics, sterile cultures, treated with ceftriaxone plus gentamicin
items.exp: 'Culture report negative : m/c condition, H/o treatment medication (antibiotics), Culture sterile, Ceftriaxone + Gentamicin'; 'Culture negative : Rare condition, No Rx, Vancomycin + Gentamicin × 4-6 wks'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Which regimen is printed for true culture-negative endocarditis?

Indications for surgery — match — 1) Native valve 2) Prosthetic valve … A) Dehiscence, increasing obstruction/regurgitation, heart failure B) Acute valvular regurgitation, fungal endocarditis, perivalvular aortic abscess
items.exp: 'Native valve : · Acute valvular regurgitation, · Fungal endocarditis, · Perivalvular aortic abscess'; 'Prosthetic valve : · Dehiscence, · Increasing obstruction/regurgitation, · Heart failure'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Which infection is listed as a native-valve indication for surgery?
Prophylaxis — who gets it? — match — 1) Valves 2) Congenital disease 3) Other … A) Unrepaired CHD, repaired CHD within 6 months B) Prosthetic valve, previous episode of IE C) Post cardiac transplant
items.exp: 'Indications : · People with prosthetic valve, · Previous episode of IE, · Post cardiac transplant, · Unrepaired CHD, Repaired CHD (within 6 months)'. (Book p1052)

items.q: For how long after repair is CHD still an indication for prophylaxis?
Procedures needing prophylaxis — match — 1) Dental 2) Respiratory tract … A) Dental procedure B) Adenoidectomy, tonsillectomy, incision and drainage of respiratory mucosa
items.exp: 'Pre-procedural prophylaxis : Dental procedure; Invasive procedures of respiratory tract : Adenoidectomy, Tonsillectomy, Incision/drainage of respiratory mucosa'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Fill up (Regimen): 'Amoxicillin ______ orally, given ______ before the procedure.'
items.exp: '· Amoxicillin 2g oral : 30-60 min before procedure'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Penicillin-allergy and parenteral options — match — 1) Oral allergy options 2) Unable to take orally 3) Allergy and unable to take orally … A) Ampicillin 2 g IV or ceftriaxone 1 g IV/IM B) Clindamycin 600 mg IV C) Azithromycin 500 mg, cephalexin 2 g or clindamycin 600 mg
items.exp: 'In penicillin allergy : Azithromycin 500 mg, Cephalexin 2g, Clindamycin 600 mg'; 'unable to take orally : Ampicillin 2g IV / ceftriaxone 1g IV or IM'; 'In penicillin allergy : Clindamycin 600 mg IV'. (Book p1052)

items.q: Dose of clindamycin printed for prophylaxis in penicillin allergy?
A patient with a prosthetic valve and penicillin allergy cannot swallow tablets before a dental extraction. Which printed regimen applies?
items.exp: Penicillin allergy plus inability to take orally: 'In penicillin allergy : Clindamycin 600 mg IV'. (Book p1052)
